page.layout: One column of running text; one marginal note in the right margin, beside the italic passage near the middle of the page. No headings, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: cernat ab æterno, est absurdum, quod tamen admittunt Remonstrantes, quando docent Deum ab æterno homines eligere quoniam credunt: at vero non absurdum, sed orthodoxum est, nos credendo efficere ut Deus nos in Christo justos declaret conscientiis nostris & pronunciet, adeoque nos credendo efficere ut cessent effectus iræ & displicentiæ Dei modo, pactioni euangelicæ, convenientissimo, quo sensu nos fidem justificationis instrumentum esse credimus, non quod fides qua opus sit nostræ justitiæ pars, sed quod fide amplectamur Christum datum à Deo nobis in justitiam fidem manu quasi apprehendere justitiam Christi aut remissionem attrahere nugas meras vocant, notitiam, assensum aut applicatione esse actionem instrumentalem vocant. Sed quia fideApol f. 112 præstita non aliter (inquiunt Rem.) consequimur remissionem peccatorum, ex promisso Dei, quam si fides veluti instrumentum à Deo data esset ad obtinendam remissionem peccatorum? instrumentum justificationis dicitur. Sed R.1.[?] Fidem instrumentum respectu Dei actu justificantis nemo nostrum dixit: at respectu justificationis passive in nostram con-scientiam terminatæ instrumentum, hoc sensu appellamus, non quod fides ulla organica causalitate Christi justitiam producat; nugantur qui hoc nobis imputent, aut quod actu reali justitiam Christi attrahat, sicut manus pauperis eleemosynam attrahat (omnis enim similitudo claudicat) sed quod impleta per Dei gratiam fidei conditione, adeoque im-pleto

page.notes: The marginal note "Apol f. 112" is printed in the right margin beside the line "fide præstita"; its placement in the transcription follows that line. "con-scientiam" is split at the line end; an underline stroke runs under the word "scientiam" in the scan, which may be a printer's or reader's mark and is not transcribed. "R.1." has a special form of R before the 1 that I could not read with certainty. The mark after "peccatorum" appears as a printed question mark and is kept as printed. The text is printed in roman with italic passages; "Remonstrantes" and the passage from "quia fide" to "dicitur." are italic.
